name: Hagia Sophia
context: Justinian's basilica, completed in 537, the largest church in the world for nearly a thousand years, a mosque in 1453, a museum in 1934, a mosque again in 2020. The studios Sébah & Joaillier and Abdullah Frères photographed it in the 19th century.

archives.title: Fonds Achille Dassonville (1890-1967) - Turquie - Istanbul - Vue de la salle de prière de la mosquée Ayasofya (MédiHAL 4161210)
archives.artist: Maison Méditerranéenne Des Sciences de l'Homme Phonothèque, Achille Fernand Hector Dassonville
archives.description: This photograph is taken from the sacred precincts of the prayer hall of the Ayasofya Mosque in Turkey. A group of people, including General Dassonville's wife, Blanche Bathurst Clarke, can clearly be seen contemplating the architecture of the hall. This mosque was once a Byzantine-era church, but was later converted into a mosque after the Ottoman capture of Constantinople. The two stereoscopic views are not identical.

currents.description: Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque, Sultan Ahmet, Ayasofya Meydanı No 1, 34122 Fatih/Istanbul, Türkiye / Turkey Hagia Sophia (“Holy Wisdom”) is an iconic and culturally significant mosque in Istanbul, Turkiye. Built as a church in 7th century, it became a mosque with the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople, then a museum, and is now a mosque again. With a gargantuan dome size, it is a masterpiece of Byzantine architecture.
